title: Probate a will or qualify as executor or administrator
question: Someone died owning property in Albemarle. How do I probate the will or qualify to handle the estate?
audience: families of people who have died
office: Clerk of the Circuit Court of Albemarle County (elected constitutional officer), Probate Division of the Albemarle Circuit Court Clerk's Office, 16th Judicial Circuit
summary: For someone who lived in Albemarle County, the Albemarle Circuit Court Clerk's Office at 350 Park Street, Court Square, probates the will and appoints the executor or administrator, by appointment only (434-972-4083). Bring the original will, a death certificate copy and asset values, and fill in the Probate Information Form (CC-1650). With no will, an heir can qualify; in the first 30 days only a sole heir or one with the others' waivers. You take an oath, give bond, file a list of heirs, and pay the state probate tax (10 cents per $100 on estates over $15,000), the county's one-third and a qualification fee. Notify heirs within 30 days. Clerk's orders can be appealed within six months.

steps.step: Confirm that the Albemarle Circuit Court is the right court
steps.who: The person holding the will, the named executor, or a family member
steps.how: Wills are probated, and administrators appointed, in the circuit court of the county or city where the person who died lived. If they lived in Albemarle County, including the Town of Scottsville, go to the Albemarle Circuit Court Clerk's Office in the County Courthouse on Court Square. If they lived in the City of Charlottesville, use the separate Charlottesville Circuit Court, even though both courthouses are in downtown Charlottesville. Moving into a nursing home or similar institution because of age or ill health is presumed, unless shown otherwise, not to change where someone lived. If the person lived in another Virginia locality, probate happens there; if they lived outside Virginia, their home court usually probates first and an authenticated copy of the will and certificate of probate can then be offered here. Usually the clerk or a deputy clerk, not a judge, handles probate. The Clerk's Office cannot give legal advice.
steps.deadline: No set deadline; the Virginia Court Clerks' Association pamphlet recommends starting the initial steps within 30 days after death. If a will leaving Virginia real estate is not offered for probate (and then admitted) within one year after the death, it does not affect the title of a good-faith buyer who bought that land from the heirs without notice of the will (Va. Code § 64.2-456).

steps.step: Until qualifying, the named executor only handles the funeral and protects the property
steps.who: The person named as executor in the will
steps.how: A named executor has no power to act for the estate until qualifying at the Clerk's Office. Before that, they may only arrange the burial, pay reasonable funeral expenses and keep property from being wasted. Keep the original will safe, because the original must be brought to the clerk.
steps.quote: A person named in a will as executor shall not exercise the powers of executor until he qualifies as such by taking an oath and giving bond in the court or before the clerk where the will or an authenticated copy thereof is admitted to record, except that he may provide for the burial of the testator, pay reasonable funeral expenses, and preserve the estate from waste.

steps.step: Check whether an executor or administrator needs to qualify at all
steps.how: The county's Probate Division page notes that probate covers only assets held solely in the decedent's name. Property owned jointly with survivorship rights, life insurance not payable to the estate, real estate passing by a transfer on death deed, and other property passing by contract or beneficiary designation is outside the probate estate. If the whole personal probate estate is $75,000 or less, at least 60 days have passed since the death, and no application to appoint an executor or administrator is pending or has been granted anywhere, all known successors can sign a Small Estate Affidavit (CC-1685), each signature notarized, and give it to whoever holds the asset, without anyone qualifying. The affidavit states that any will was duly probated, so a will still has to be probated at the Clerk's Office; the clerk can probate a will without appointing anyone.
steps.deadline: At least 60 days after the death (small estate affidavit)
steps.quote: this form should only be used when the value of the deceased person’s entire personal probate estate as of the date of death does not exceed $75,000.

steps.step: Call the Clerk's Office Probate Division for an appointment
steps.who: The person offering the will, or the person asking to be appointed
steps.how: At the Albemarle Circuit Court Clerk's Office, probating a will and qualifying an executor or administrator are done only by appointment, because the process can take an hour or more. Call the Clerk's Office at 434-972-4083 and ask for the Probate Division to schedule and to find out what will be needed. Clerk's Office hours are 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. The county's Clerk's Office page also said, in a copy of May 2026, that the office was closed to public traffic, so do not go without an appointment. The clerk may give you forms to fill in before the appointment.

steps.step: Fill in the Probate Information Form and gather what to bring
steps.who: The person offering the will, or the person asking to be appointed
steps.how: Fill in as much of the Probate Information Form (CC-1650) as you can; the clerk will help with the rest. Bring the original will and every codicil, a copy of the death certificate, and a list of the assets with values as accurate as you can make them. Count only the probate estate (see step s3).
steps.quote: Be sure to bring all originals of the will and any codicils with you when you come to the courthouse.

steps.step: Prove that the will was properly signed
steps.who: The person offering the will, with the will's witnesses if needed
steps.how: If the will has a self-proving affidavit (the testator and witnesses signed a sworn statement before a notary), no witness has to come. If it does not, bring at least one of the will's witnesses. For a will written entirely in the testator's handwriting, bring two disinterested people (not relatives, beneficiaries or relatives of beneficiaries) who know the handwriting; they swear to the Proof of Holographic Will (CC-1604) before the clerk or a deputy clerk (the same form proves the will of a person in military service). A witness who lives outside Virginia, or who cannot come to the courthouse because of sickness, age, legal confinement or another cause, can instead give a deposition before a notary public: CC-1601 for a witness to a will without a self-proving clause, CC-1602 for a witness to a handwritten will, and CC-1603 to prove the signatures of attesting witnesses who have died and of the testator. The clerk may require all of the testator's will papers to be produced.
steps.quote: If a will has a self-proving affidavit, it is not necessary for any witnesses to come to the Clerk’s Office.

steps.step: If there is no will, or the named executor will not serve, work out who may be appointed
steps.who: Heirs (distributees), residuary or substantial beneficiaries, creditors
steps.how: With no will: in the first 30 days after death the clerk may appoint only a sole heir, or an heir who brings written waivers (CC-1608) from all the other competent heirs. After 30 days, the first heir who applies may be appointed, but if more than one heir told the clerk within those 30 days that they mean to qualify, all of them must be heard first. After 45 days, a nonprofit charitable organization that was the decedent's conservator or guardian may be appointed after the same kind of search and notice. After 60 days, a creditor or another person may be appointed after certifying a diligent search and a certified-mail notice to any sole heir at least 30 days before applying, or that no address could be found (CC-1609). If the will names no executor, or the executor declines, a residuary or substantial beneficiary may be appointed administrator with the will annexed; if none applies within 30 days, a person who would inherit without a will may be. Anyone appointed must be suitable and competent and not under a legal disability. An administrator of an estate with no will must also sign under oath that they are not under a disability and have not been convicted of certain felonies (such as fraud, robbery, larceny, embezzlement or perjury); a sole heir with such a conviction may still be appointed if otherwise suitable and competent. The Probate Information Form (CC-1650) asks these questions, and its instructions say a yes answer does not by itself disqualify anyone.
steps.deadline: First 30 days after death: sole heir, or an heir with waivers; after 30 days: first heir who applies; after 45 days: a nonprofit that was the decedent's conservator or guardian; after 60 days: creditor or other person
steps.quote: After 30 days have passed since the decedent's death, the court or the clerk may grant administration to the first distributee, or his designee, who applies

steps.step: File the probate tax return and pay the state and county probate tax
steps.who: The person offering the will or asking for administration; the Clerk collects it
steps.how: If the estate is worth more than $15,000, file the confidential Probate Tax Return (CC-1651) with the clerk. Give the value of Virginia real estate (the local assessed value is accepted if you do not know the actual value) and a reasonable estimate of the personal property as of the date of death. Pay the state tax and the Albemarle County tax, which is one-third of the state tax, at the Clerk's Office; the clerk collects the county tax and pays it into the county treasury. No one can qualify until the tax is paid. If the later inventory shows a higher value, the clerk collects the extra tax.
steps.deadline: At the time the will is offered for probate or administration is sought
steps.fee: State: 10 cents per $100 of value or fraction of $100 (no tax on estates of $15,000 or less); Albemarle County: one-third of the state tax (Albemarle County Code § 15-500)
steps.quote: No one shall be permitted to qualify and act as executor or administrator until the tax imposed by § 58.1-1712 has been paid.

steps.step: Take the oath and sign the bond
steps.who: The executor or administrator, before the clerk or a deputy clerk
steps.how: You swear to carry out the duties faithfully and sign a bond for at least the value of the personal estate (plus real estate if the will lets you sell it). Surety is required unless the will waives it or every heir or beneficiary is serving as personal representative; the clerk may also allow a bond without surety when no more than $35,000 will come into your hands. Surety is normally a surety bond bought from an insurance company and paid for from estate assets. A person who does not live in Virginia must file a written consent to service of process (CC-1610) and must give bond with surety even if the will waives surety, unless a Virginia resident qualifies at the same time or the clerk waives surety under the $35,000 rule. Pay the qualification fee.
steps.fee: Qualification fee: $20 for estates up to $50,000, $25 up to $100,000, $30 over $100,000; no fee for estates of $5,000 or less (statutory). Any surety bond premium is extra.
steps.quote: The court or clerk shall require a personal representative to furnish security.

steps.who: The executor or administrator (or the person offering the will if no one qualifies)
steps.how: Sign the List of Heirs (CC-1611) under oath, giving every heir at law with address, relationship and age, whether or not there is a will. File it with the clerk when you qualify, and with the clerk of any other city or county where the decedent's real estate lies. You cannot be paid for your work until it is filed, unless you file an affidavit with the Commissioner of Accounts that the heirs are unknown to you after diligent inquiry. If no one has qualified within 30 days of the death of a person without a will, an heir may file a list of heirs alone.
steps.deadline: At the time of qualification (or when the will is presented, if no one qualifies)
steps.fee: Recording cost is paid from the estate. When no will is probated and no administration is granted, recording a list of heirs costs a $25 state fee plus a $25 Albemarle County tax.
steps.quote: furnish a list of heirs under oath in accordance with a form provided to each clerk of court by the Office of the Executive Secretary of the Supreme Court

steps.step: Get the probate order and certificate of qualification
steps.who: Clerk of the Albemarle Circuit Court or a deputy clerk
steps.how: The clerk enters the order admitting the will and appointing you and records the will in the will book. The clerk may issue a certificate of qualification, which the law gives the same effect as letters of administration or probate made out in due form; banks and others use it as proof that you can act for the estate. The clerk also gives you a written statement that you are responsible for filing tax returns and accounting for the estate, and the notice forms for the next step. Ask how many certified copies you need.
steps.fee: Copies: $0.50 per page; $2 for attaching the court seal and clerk's certificate (statutory amounts)
steps.quote: The court or clerk may issue a certificate of qualification to any personal representative for obtaining probate or letters of administration, which shall be given the same effect as the probate or letters made out in due form.

steps.step: Send notice to the spouse, heirs and beneficiaries
steps.who: The executor or administrator, or the person who probated the will
steps.how: Use the Notice Regarding Estate (CC-1616). Deliver it, or mail it first-class, to the surviving spouse, all heirs at law (even when there is a will), the living beneficiaries under the will (including beneficiaries of a trust the will creates) and the living beneficiaries under any earlier will of the decedent probated in the same court, at their last known addresses. The notice gives the Albemarle Circuit Court Clerk's mailing address and that of the Commissioner of Accounts. Anyone who signed a Waiver of Notice (CC-1618), anyone already summoned to a show-cause hearing on the will, and a non-heir whose gift is $10,000 or less of money or personal belongings do not need one. The notice tells them they may ask for copies of the inventory and accounts.
steps.deadline: Within 30 days after the date of qualification or admission of the will to probate
steps.quote: Within 30 days after the date of qualification or admission of the will to probate, a personal representative or proponent of the will shall forward notice by delivery or by first-class mail, postage prepaid, to the persons entitled to notice at their last known address.

steps.who: The executor or administrator, or the person who probated the will
steps.how: Sign the Affidavit of Notice Regarding Estate (CC-1617), listing who was sent the notice and when, or stating that no notice was required, and record it at the Albemarle Circuit Court Clerk's Office. The Commissioner of Accounts cannot approve the estate's settlement until it is recorded, and summons a fiduciary who has not done it after four months.
steps.deadline: Within four months (after qualification or probate)
steps.quote: The personal representative or proponent of the will shall record within four months in the clerk's office where the will is recorded an affidavit stating

steps.step: Record the will and list of heirs wherever the decedent's Virginia real estate lies
steps.how: If the decedent owned, or left by will, real estate in another Virginia city or county, record a certified copy of the will at that circuit court clerk's office, and file the list of heirs there too. The same applies in reverse: when someone who lived elsewhere in Virginia owned land in Albemarle, the will probated at home is recorded, and the list of heirs filed, at the Albemarle Circuit Court Clerk's Office. When there was no will, anyone with an interest in the decedent's real estate may record a Real Estate Affidavit (CC-1612) where the land lies, so the land records show the heirs.
steps.fee: Recording fee by page count (statutory); $25 state fee plus $25 Albemarle County tax for a real estate affidavit when no will is probated and no administration is granted
steps.quote: The personal representative of the testator shall cause a certified copy of any will or of any authenticated copy so admitted to record to be recorded in any county or city wherein there is any real estate of which the testator possessed at the time of his death or that is devised by his will.

steps.step: File the inventory with the Commissioner of Accounts
steps.who: The executor or administrator; reviewed by the Commissioner of Accounts appointed by the Albemarle Circuit Court
steps.how: List the estate's assets at their value on the date of death on the Inventory for Decedent's Estate (CC-1670) and file it with the Commissioner of Accounts (the statewide directory lists the Albemarle commissioners, or ask the clerk). Mail a copy to each entitled person who asked in writing for one. The commissioner charges a filing fee set by the court. The clerk compares the inventory with the probate tax return and collects any additional tax.
steps.deadline: Within four months after the date of the order conferring authority (qualification)
steps.fee: Commissioner of Accounts filing fee, set by the Albemarle Circuit Court
steps.quote: Every personal representative or curator shall, within four months after the date of the order conferring his authority, return to the commissioner of accounts an inventory of all the personal estate under his supervision and control

steps.step: File accounts until the estate is settled
steps.how: File the first account (CC-1680) with the Commissioner of Accounts, covering the first 12 months, then an account for each later year until the estate is settled. When every heir or residuary beneficiary is also a personal representative, a Statement in Lieu of Settlement of Account (CC-1681) may be filed instead once debts are paid, six months have passed and the estate is distributed. If that statement cannot be filed within the 16 months, file an interim account or a sworn notice of intent instead. If you move out of Virginia while serving, tell the clerk and the Commissioner of Accounts your new address within 30 days (not needed when a co-fiduciary lives in Virginia), or a $50 civil penalty applies. File the income, inheritance or estate tax returns the law requires.
steps.deadline: Within 16 months from the date of qualification; later accounts within four months after the end of each 12-month period
steps.fee: Commissioner of Accounts filing fee, set by the Albemarle Circuit Court
steps.quote: Within 16 months from the date of the qualification, personal representatives shall exhibit before the commissioner of accounts a statement of all money and other property that the fiduciary has received, has become chargeable with, or has disbursed within 12 months from the date of qualification.

fees.item: Albemarle County tax in lieu of probate tax (recording a list of heirs or a real estate affidavit for an intestate decedent when no will is probated and no administration is granted)
fees.quote: A tax of $25.00 is hereby imposed for the recordation of a list of heirs or an affidavit listing real estate owned by an intestate decedent.

fees.item: Additional probate tax (or refund) after the inventory shows a different value
fees.amount: The difference; none charged or refunded if under $25
fees.quote: No additional tax shall be payable or no refund made if the payment or refund due would be less than twenty-five dollars.

fees.item: Copies of court papers (for example the will or the qualification order)
fees.quote: For making out a copy of any paper, record, or electronic record to go out of the office, which is not otherwise specifically provided for herein, a fee of $0.50 for each page or, if an electronic record, each image.

fees.item: Court seal and clerk's certificate on a copy (certified copy)
fees.amount: $2 (plus $0.50 if the judge's certificate is requested)
fees.quote: For annexing the seal of the court to any paper, writing the certificate of the clerk accompanying it, the clerk shall charge $2

fees.item: Surety bond premium (when surety is not waived)
fees.amount: Set by the surety company; paid from estate assets
fees.quote: This is normally done by purchasing a surety bond from an insurance company and paying for it out of estate assets.

fees.item: Commissioner of Accounts fees (inventory, accounts, statements in lieu)
fees.amount: Set by the Albemarle Circuit Court; no Albemarle schedule was found. The statewide guideline effective January 1, 2023 lists, for example, $135.00 to $350.00 for an inventory and $275.00 to $1,650.00 (plus .00075 over $1,000,000) for a first account, by asset value, and $250.00 for a statement in lieu of settlement.
fees.quote: By statute, each Circuit Court sets the fees for its Commissioner(s) of Accounts

escalation.trigger: The clerk refuses to admit the will or to appoint you, or you disagree with the clerk's probate or appointment order
escalation.next: Albemarle Circuit Court (a judge), which hears the matter anew (de novo)
escalation.deadline: Within six months after the clerk's order
escalation.quote: Any person interested in the probate of the will may appeal any order entered pursuant to § 64.2-444 within six months after the entering of such an order, without giving any bond, to the circuit court whose clerk, or deputy, has made the order.

escalation.trigger: More than one heir wants to be administrator
escalation.next: The clerk or the court, which must give every heir who gave notice an opportunity to be heard before appointing anyone
escalation.deadline: Notify the clerk during the first 30 days after the death
escalation.quote: more than one distributee notifies the court or the clerk of an intent to qualify after the 30-day period has elapsed, the court or the clerk shall not grant administration to any distributee, or his designee, until the court or the clerk has given all such distributees an opportunity to be heard.

escalation.trigger: The order of appointment in the statute would not serve the estate
escalation.next: Albemarle Circuit Court, which may appoint another suitable person
escalation.quote: if the court determines that it is in the best interests of a decedent's estate, the court may depart from the provisions of this section at any time and grant administration to such person as the court deems appropriate.

escalation.trigger: The will's validity is doubtful or a dispute is expected before probate
escalation.next: Ask the clerk to summon everyone interested to show cause why the will should not be probated; the Albemarle Circuit Court then hears the motion (with a jury if anyone interested asks)
escalation.quote: may request that the clerk of such court summon any person interested in the probate of the will to appear to show cause why the will should not be admitted to probate.

escalation.trigger: Estate property is at risk while the will is contested or before anyone qualifies
escalation.next: Ask the clerk or the Albemarle Circuit Court to appoint a curator to protect the estate
escalation.quote: may appoint a curator of the estate of a decedent during a contest about the decedent's will, during the infancy or in the absence of an executor, or until administration of the estate be granted

escalation.trigger: An interested person who was not part of the clerk's proceeding wants to contest the will, or to establish a will
escalation.next: Complaint to impeach or establish the will in circuit court (jury trial)
escalation.deadline: Within one year from the clerk's or court's order (two years if served only by order of publication)
escalation.quote: may file a complaint to impeach or establish the will within one year from the date of the order entered by the court in exercise of its original jurisdiction

escalation.trigger: An heir or beneficiary thinks the estate needs a bond with surety after surety was waived
escalation.next: Motion to the Albemarle Circuit Court to require the personal representative to furnish security (a hearing is held)
escalation.quote: upon the motion of a legatee, devisee, or distributee of an estate, or any person who has a pecuniary interest in an estate, the court or clerk may require the personal representative to furnish security.

escalation.trigger: No affidavit of notice is recorded within four months after qualification
escalation.next: Commissioner of Accounts, who summons the fiduciary and enforces the filing
escalation.quote: If this subsection has not been complied with within four months after qualification, the commissioner of accounts shall issue, through the sheriff or other proper officer, a summons to such fiduciary requiring him to comply

escalation.trigger: The executor or administrator does not file the inventory within four months
escalation.next: Commissioner of Accounts summons the fiduciary; if it is still not filed 30 days after service, the commissioner reports to the Albemarle Circuit Court, which summons the fiduciary and must fine them up to $500 unless excused for sufficient reason; continued failure is punished as contempt of court
escalation.quote: the commissioner of accounts shall issue, through the sheriff or other proper officer, a summons to the fiduciary requiring him to make such return.

escalation.trigger: An heir or beneficiary disagrees with the executor's or administrator's inventory or account
escalation.next: Object before the Commissioner of Accounts
escalation.quote: Any interested person, or the next friend of an interested person, may, before the commissioner of accounts, insist upon or object to anything

escalation.trigger: You disagree with the Commissioner of Accounts' report on an account
escalation.next: File exceptions; the Albemarle Circuit Court examines them and corrects errors
escalation.deadline: Before the report stands confirmed, 15 days after it is filed in the clerk's office
escalation.quote: If no exceptions have been filed, the report shall stand confirmed on the day next following the expiration of the period of 15 days

escalation.trigger: A Commissioner of Accounts fails to perform, or violates, a statutory duty
escalation.next: Written complaint to the Standing Committee on Commissioners of Accounts of the Judicial Council of Virginia, sent to the Executive Secretary of the Supreme Court of Virginia
escalation.basis: Rules for Addressing Complaints Against Commissioners of Accounts (Judicial Council of Virginia, effective April 1, 2021), https://www.vacourts.gov/static/courts/circuit/resources/coa/coa_complaints.pdf
escalation.quote: All Complaints shall be submitted in writing to the Executive Secretary of the Supreme Court of Virginia

escalation.trigger: Probate tax was overpaid (the inventory shows a lower value than the probate tax return)
escalation.next: Refund application to the Virginia Department of Taxation for the state share and, for the county share, to the county officer with treasurer duties (in Albemarle, the Director of Finance, Department of Finance & Budget)
escalation.quote: In the event of an overpayment of such tax, the personal representative may apply to the Department of Taxation and, if a local probate tax was paid, to the treasurer of the city or county for a refund.

escalation.trigger: The Albemarle Circuit Court enters a final order you believe is wrong
escalation.next: Court of Appeals of Virginia (notice of appeal)
escalation.deadline: Within 30 days from the date of the final order
escalation.quote: a notice of appeal to the Court of Appeals in any case within the jurisdiction of the court shall be filed within 30 days from the date of any final judgment order

escalation.trigger: You need a disability accommodation at the Clerk's Office, or one is refused
escalation.next: The Clerk of the Albemarle Circuit Court; other complaints go through the Office of the Executive Secretary's ADA grievance procedure
escalation.quote: Complaints concerning a program, service, or activity of a circuit court clerk's office should be directed to that clerk.

caveats: Albemarle County's website (www.albemarle.org) refuses automated readers, so the county pages and PDFs cited here are Internet Archive copies: they show the pages as they were when copied. One is the County-published Chapter 15 (Taxation) PDF of 2019-09-18, which is no longer on the county site. The live pages may have changed since; confirm on them before you act. The County's Terms and Conditions bar reposting its content without written permission, so the County's own words are not reprinted on this page; each step links the County page instead.

The county's Probate Division page describes probate only briefly (venue, appointment only, phone). The detailed steps come from state law and the statewide Office of the Executive Secretary forms and instructions, which note possible local variations. What the Albemarle office asks you to bring beyond the original will, death certificate and asset values, how many certified copies it suggests, and which payment methods it accepts were not found; ask when booking.

Privacy: the Probate Division page names two staff members, asks callers to reach them at an extension of the main line, and links a personal mailbox for one of them; the Clerk's Office page's 'Email the Department' link goes to a personal-looking mailbox of the elected Clerk. None of these are recorded: no staff or Clerk names, no mailbox and no extension (the extension is given as the way to reach the two named staff members, so it is treated as a staff line). No general office mailbox for probate was found. Call the Clerk's Office main line and ask for the Probate Division.

Venue matters here. An Albemarle County resident's will (including a resident of the Town of Scottsville) goes to the Albemarle Circuit Court; a Charlottesville resident's goes to the separate Charlottesville Circuit Court, even though both courthouses are in downtown Charlottesville. If the person who died lived elsewhere but owned Albemarle land, probate happens where they lived, and the Albemarle clerk's role is recording a certified copy of the will and the list of heirs (§§ 64.2-455(B), 64.2-509(A)). Probate of out-of-state wills (§ 64.2-450) is summarised only.

Local law: Albemarle County Code §§ 15-500 to 15-502 are quoted from the County's own Chapter 15 PDF (marked Supp. #41, 1-19, amended through Ord. 19-15(1) of April 17, 2019), read from an Internet Archive copy of 2019-09-18; the PDF is no longer on the county site. The County Code page now points to Municode, which was not read (its terms of use were not confirmed). A search of Albemarle's Legistar matter titles (webapi.legistar.com) for 'probate', 'heirs' and 'Chapter 15' found the 2017 ordinance adding the $25 tax in lieu (matter 17-541, passed October 4, 2017) and no later matter naming Article 5 or probate; the title of a March 2020 emergency ordinance amending Chapter 15 does not say what it changed. Confirm the current text before relying on it.

§ 15-501's text does not repeat the condition that the $25 county tax applies only when no will has been probated and no administration granted. The Legistar summary of the 2017 ordinance and Va. Code § 58.1-1717.1 state that condition, so the $25 state fee and the $25 county tax are treated here as charged only in that case.

Who receives the county share: § 58.1-3806 has the clerk pay the county tax into the county treasury, and Albemarle has no elected Treasurer; its Director of Finance has the treasurer's duties (§ 15.2-522), and County Code § 15-100(B) (2019 text) gives the Director, in administering Chapter 15 (which includes the probate tax article), the powers and duties of treasurers under general law. Sending a county-share refund request to the Department of Finance & Budget is an inference from those sections; no county page on probate tax refunds was found.

Office access: the county's Circuit Court Clerk's Office page (Internet Archive copy of 2026-05-09) says the office is closed to public traffic, while the court's vacourts.gov page lists Clerk's Office hours of 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. and the Probate Division page says probate is done solely by appointment. The notice may be left over from the 2020 closure (the county's Documents Center lists a Clerk's Office COVID-19 order), but that was not confirmed; call before going.

The 'Guide to the Administration of Decedents' Estates in Virginia' linked from the county's Clerk pages is the Virginia Bar Association's 2005 revision. It predates the 2012 recodification into Title 64.2 and current amounts (for example the $75,000 small-asset limit), so it is listed as background only and not quoted.

The 'Probate in Virginia' pamphlet (Virginia Court Clerks' Association, republished July 2019, hosted on vacourts.gov) gives a $50,000 limit for small-asset estates. Current Va. Code § 64.2-601(A)(1) and the CC-1685 Small Estate Affidavit (revised 07/26) say $75,000. The pamphlet's probate tax figures ($1.00 state and .33 local per $1,000) match 10 cents per $100 plus one-third.

The CC-1651 Probate Tax Return's preparation note says the form 'must be completed if the value of the estate exceeds $10,000', but the form itself and Va. Code § 58.1-1714 say $15,000. The statute governs.

Some statewide instructions are old: CC-1650 instructions are dated 07/03 and 07/13 and quote an earlier wording of the nursing-home presumption, CC-1680 instructions are dated 11/06, and CC-1608 instructions cite repealed §§ 64.1-1 and 64.1-11 (now in Title 64.2).

Clerk fees: the Albemarle clerk publishes no itemized probate fee list on the pages read. The fees given are the statutory amounts. How the clerk applies recording fees to wills and lists of heirs, whether it charges the $3 bond fee in § 17.1-275(A)(6), and whether cards are accepted (the law allows a convenience fee of up to 4 percent or $2, § 17.1-275(A)(27)) were not confirmed. The county's Clerk 'Online Payment' page links only to the state payment system for fines, costs and restitution.
Hours: 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. is from the Albemarle Circuit Court page on vacourts.gov; the county pages read do not list hours.

Commissioner of Accounts: the Albemarle Circuit Court's own commissioner fee schedule was not found. The amounts given are the statewide Uniform Fee Schedule Guidelines, which the vacourts.gov page says to confirm with the local circuit court. The statewide directory (updated as of 8/31/2026) lists commissioners for Albemarle; they are individual attorneys, so no names or contact details are recorded. Use the directory or ask the clerk.

Not covered in detail: administrators appointed only for wrongful death or personal injury suits (§ 64.2-454), curators beyond the escalation note (§ 64.2-451), guardianships and conservatorships (also handled by the Probate Division), corporate fiduciaries, estate debts and creditor claims, and federal or state income and estate tax returns.

County site terms: the archived Terms and Conditions authorise browsing for information but restrict reposting site content without written permission. County-page quotes here are single short sentences with their source; check reuse before republishing more.

removed: No quote was removed: all 98 original quotes were confirmed.

Contacts and s4: the Probate Division extension was removed. The county page gives it as the way to reach two named staff members, so under the contact rules (docs/design/entities-contacts.md, section 5) it is a staff line. The Clerk's Office main line 434-972-4083 is kept, with 'ask for the Probate Division'.
corrections: Quotes: all 98 original quotes were checked. The 84 state-law quotes are substrings of I.text_of for the cited section (whitespace normalised), and every cited subsection label matches the text. The 14 local and procedure quotes were matched word for word against Internet Archive copies of the albemarle.org Probate Division page (2026-03-17) and the County's Chapter 15 PDF (2019-09-18), re-fetched on 2026-10-11 (www.albemarle.org still answers HTTP 403, robots.txt included, and was not circumvented), and against the vacourts.gov PDFs fetched the same day (CC-1650 and CC-1685 instructions, the Commissioner of Accounts fee guidelines and complaint rules, the Circuit Courts Informational Pamphlet). Legistar matter 17-541 (passed 2017-10-04) was confirmed through the Legistar Web API.

Added and checked the same way (now 106 quotes; lexflow's check_quotes gives 91 of 91 state quotes matched): Va. Code §§ 64.2-403(B) (two disinterested witnesses for a handwritten will), 64.2-447(A) (depositions of witnesses), 64.2-456 (one-year rule protecting buyers from heirs), 64.2-502(D) (sole-heir exception to the felony bar), 64.2-601(A)(3) (no pending or granted appointment), 64.2-1409(B) (30-day notice of a move out of Virginia; $50 penalty), and Albemarle County Code § 15-100(B) (Director of Finance has treasurers' powers in administering Chapter 15). Two confirmed quotes were extended to carry the conditions the steps now state: § 64.2-1426(A) (surety waiver only under § 64.2-1411) and § 64.2-509(D) (the unknown-heirs affidavit exception).

s6 and forms: CC-1604 is not a deposition. It is the Proof of Holographic Will / Proof of Will of Person in Military Service, sworn before the clerk or a deputy clerk. The step now says so and names CC-1601, CC-1602 and CC-1603 as the deposition forms, and the f10 title now matches the form. 'Legal confinement' was added from the CC-1650 instructions.

s7: the draft said everyone appointed must swear they have not been convicted of certain felonies. That oath is in § 64.2-502(D), for administration of an intestate estate, and has a sole-heir exception. For administration with the will annexed, § 64.2-500(B) bars only persons under a disability. The step now says this, adds the 45-day nonprofit conservator or guardian rung (§ 64.2-502(A)(3)), and notes that the CC-1650 instructions say a yes answer does not by itself disqualify anyone. Deadline updated to match.

s9: § 64.2-1426(A) requires a nonresident to give surety notwithstanding § 64.2-505, so a will's waiver does not help. The only waiver is under § 64.2-1411 (the $35,000 rule). The draft said only that 'the clerk waives surety'.

s3: adds the § 64.2-601(A)(3) and CC-1685 condition that no application to appoint a personal representative is pending or has been granted, and says each successor's signature must be notarized (CC-1685 instructions).

s16: the draft told fiduciaries to tell the commissioner at once if their address or phone number changes. No source for that was found in the CC-1680 or CC-1670 instructions, the Commissioner of Accounts page or the Code. It is replaced with § 64.2-1409(B): a fiduciary who moves out of Virginia must tell the clerk and the commissioner within 30 days (unless a co-fiduciary lives in Virginia), or a $50 civil penalty applies. Also adds the § 64.2-1314(C) interim account or notice of intent when a statement in lieu cannot be filed within the 16 months.

s1: the nursing-home presumption is now described as rebuttable and limited to moves because of age or ill health (§ 64.2-443(B)). The deadline adds § 64.2-456: a will leaving Virginia real estate that is not offered for probate within one year does not affect a good-faith buyer from the heirs. The draft gave no deadline.

s11: § 64.2-506 says the clerk 'may issue' a certificate of qualification; the draft said 'issues'. s10: adds the § 64.2-509(D) exception to the bar on compensation. s12: adds the trust beneficiaries and earlier-will beneficiaries of § 64.2-508(A)(3) and (4), and the § 64.2-508(B)(3) exemption for persons summoned under § 64.2-446.
Escalation rung 9 (inventory not filed): § 64.2-1215(A) says the court 'shall' fine the fiduciary up to $500 unless excused, and continued failure is contempt. The draft said the court 'can fine'.

Caveats: privacy caveat updated for the dropped extension. New caveat: the county's Clerk's Office page (copy of 2026-05-09) says the office is closed to public traffic. The county-share refund caveat now also cites County Code § 15-100(B). Four sources added for the new sections.

Also confirmed, with no change needed: hours (8:00AM - 4:00PM), main line, fax and address from the vacourts.gov Albemarle Circuit Court page; that the county Clerk page says the office cannot give legal advice; the Clerks' Association pamphlet's 30-day recommendation and $50,000 figure; the CC-1651 $10,000 note; the CC-1685 revision 07/26; the 2005 Bar Association guide; the COA fee guideline amounts and the 8/31/2026 directory date; the Online Payment page linking only to the state fines and costs system; the County Code page pointing to Municode; and the archived Terms and Conditions. All 18 form URLs return the PDF on GET (vacourts.gov answers HEAD with 403). No staff names or personal mailboxes are in the file.
open_issues: County Code §§ 15-100, 15-500 to 15-502 are quoted from the County's 2019 Chapter 15 PDF (an Internet Archive copy). The current text on Municode was not read, and the live albemarle.org pages could not be read (HTTP 403). Legistar title searches found no later change to the probate article.

The Albemarle clerk's fee practice is not confirmed: how recording fees apply to wills and lists of heirs, whether the $3 bond fee is charged, and whether cards are accepted. The Albemarle Commissioner of Accounts fee schedule was not found; the statewide 2023 guidelines are given instead.
The 'closed to public traffic' notice on the county Clerk page (copy of 2026-05-09) may be stale; the appointment-only instruction in s4 does not depend on it.

Sending a refund request for the county share to the Department of Finance & Budget is still an inference (from §§ 58.1-1717, 15.2-522 and County Code § 15-100(B)); no county page on probate tax refunds was found.
Whether the short county-page and County Code quotes may be republished under the county's Terms and Conditions is for the project owner to decide.
